title: Build Once, Deploy Many: CI/CD Container Images
summary: Quick revision notes on building a container image once in CI and promoting that exact artifact through every environment. Covers tags vs digests, multi-stage builds, layer caching, registries, scanning and promotion.

chapters.title: Build Once, Deploy Many: The Mental Model
points: Build once, deploy many: CI builds the image a single time and every environment runs that exact artifact
Rebuilding per environment gives different bytes for the same commit, so staging proves nothing about prod
Environment differences live in runtime config (env vars, secrets, mounted config), never baked into the image
An image is a stack of immutable layers plus a manifest; the manifest hash is its identity
Pipeline shape: build → test → scan → push → promote (dev → staging → prod)

chapters.title: Tags vs Immutable Digests
points: A tag is a mutable pointer: myapp:1.4 can be re-pushed to point at different content
A digest (sha256:...) is the hash of the manifest, so it is immutable and content-addressed
Reference by digest: docker pull myapp@sha256:<digest>; the form myapp:1.4@sha256:<digest> pins the digest and the tag is only a label
Tag with the git SHA (myapp:3f9c2ab) for traceability; avoid :latest in any deployed manifest
Read the digest after push: docker buildx imagetools inspect myapp:3f9c2ab or docker inspect --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}'
Enable tag immutability on the registry (e.g. ECR immutable tags) so re-pushing an existing tag is rejected

chapters.title: Multi-Stage Builds and Layer Caching in CI
points: Multi-stage: FROM node:22 AS build compiles, then FROM node:22-slim copies only artifacts via COPY --from=build /app/dist ./dist
Final stage drops compilers and dev dependencies, so the image is smaller with a smaller attack surface
Layer order for cache hits: base image, then COPY package*.json and install deps, then COPY source last
A changed layer invalidates every layer after it, so put the slowest-changing steps first
CI runners are ephemeral, so the local cache is empty: use docker buildx build --cache-from type=registry,ref=myapp:cache --cache-to type=registry,ref=myapp:cache,mode=max
Alternatives: type=gha for GitHub Actions cache; BuildKit cache mounts (RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.npm) for package managers
A .dockerignore (node_modules, .git, .env) keeps the build context small and stops secrets leaking into layers

chapters.title: Registries, Retention and Image Scanning
points: Registry stores images by repository, tag and digest (ECR, GHCR, Docker Hub, Harbor); CI pushes with a short-lived credential, not a personal password
Retention/lifecycle policies expire untagged and old images, e.g. ECR: keep the last 30 images, expire untagged after 7 days
Never expire the digests currently deployed in any environment, or rollbacks and pod restarts fail with ImagePullBackOff
Scan in CI before push or promotion with Trivy or Grype: trivy image --severity HIGH,CRITICAL --exit-code 1 myapp:3f9c2ab
Registry scan on push (ECR basic or enhanced scanning) plus periodic rescans, because new CVEs appear for images already deployed
Scan results attach to a digest, not a tag, so a gate result stays valid only for that exact image
Sign images (cosign) and verify the signature at deploy time to prove the digest came from your pipeline

chapters.title: Promoting the Same Image Across Environments
points: Promotion moves the same digest forward; it never rebuilds: dev → staging → prod
Promote by retagging the existing manifest: docker buildx imagetools create -t myapp:prod myapp@sha256:<digest>, which copies no layers
Deploy manifests reference the digest, e.g. image: myapp@sha256:<digest> in a Kubernetes Deployment
GitOps promotion: a pipeline or PR bumps the digest in the env's manifest or Helm values; Git history is the audit trail and rollback is a revert
Gate each promotion on tests, scan result and approval; the gate evaluates the digest it will deploy
Per-environment config via env vars, ConfigMaps, Secrets or a secrets manager injected at runtime
Rollback means redeploying the previous digest, which is only possible if retention kept it

chapters.title: Common Mistakes and Cheat Sheet
points: Mistake: rebuilding in each environment's pipeline, so prod runs an image no test ever saw
Mistake: deploying :latest or a mutable tag, so pods on different nodes run different code
Mistake: baking secrets or env-specific config into layers, which stay readable in image history
Mistake: building without registry cache in CI, so every run reinstalls all dependencies
Cheat sheet: build once → tag with git SHA → push → record digest → scan → deploy by digest → promote via retag or manifest bump → retain deployed digests
